findings.text: the entry point cited for the request probe, _request_lane_availability at resumption.py:277, is not there - the definition is at :207 and its only call site at :301; it is the only citation in the map that failed resolution.

the enumerated non-landing departures (blocked 146, abandoned 124, dispatched 61, stopped 31, failed 21, working 10) sum to 393, not the stated 401; a seventh state, stalled (~8 rows at the stamp), is omitted from the parenthetical, so the breakdown and its headline disagree.

the map's content is unguarded - no test reads it and the crew/reports directory is not a git repository, so a later edit to a verdict or a citation can silently contradict the tree it describes; the same weakness was recorded in the review of the sibling map r-20260914T125035036163.

justifications.durability: nothing reads the record - no test asserts over the crew/reports directory (a tests/ grep finds only a fixture string naming an unrelated module and a browser probe of a different file) and the directory carries no git history, so an edited verdict or a dead citation fails nothing.

justifications.fit: the map follows the reuse-map idiom of its precedent crew/reports/display-reuse-map.md with a settled satisfied/partial/absent vocabulary and per-section write-path tables naming asserting test files beside each source, and introduces no forbidden label in its filename; it is docked for the internal §19 M1 breakdown that does not foot to its own headline.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the map carries one row per measure row of §18/§19/§20 at the base revision, verified at docs/plans/crew-observability-truth.html:888-890, :921-923 and :958-960, each with a satisfied/partial/absent verdict and a file:line citation on every satisfied and partial verdict plus a per-section write-path set with the asserting test files named, meeting the done-when; docked because its §19 M1 row sums its enumerated non-landing states to 393 against a stated 401.
